cards.text: Remember Gabriel, the angel who just told Zechariah he'd finally be a dad (Luke 1:13, 19)? In the sixth month, God sends Gabriel out AGAIN, this time to a town in Galilee. Two huge announcements back to back, and some days I can't get ONE batch out the door.

cards.question: God sends the angel Gabriel to a town in Galilee called ___.
Gabriel is headed to a virgin named Mary. True or false: Mary is already married to Joseph, a man from the house of David.

cards.text: The angel appears to Mary and says, “Greetings, you who are highly favored! The Lord is with you.” Friend, the nicest greeting I ever got in that junk drawer was somebody digging past me yelling, 'WHERE is the TAPE?'

cards.question: An angel just showed up and called Mary highly favored. True or false: Mary is perfectly calm about this greeting.

cards.text: Mary is greatly troubled, wondering what kind of greeting this even is. So Gabriel tells her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.”

cards.question: Gabriel tells Mary she will conceive and give birth to a ___, and she is to name the baby ___.

cards.text: Gabriel keeps going: this baby will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The first time an angel said 'the Most High' to ME, I looked up and said, 'The most WHO?'

cards.question: Gabriel says the Lord God will give Mary's son a throne. Whose throne?

answers.text: The throne of His father David
The throne of Herod king of Judea
The throne of Caesar in Rome

cards.question: Mary's son will reign over the house of Jacob. True or false: Gabriel says His kingdom will one day come to an end.

cards.text: A batch of my cookies has never once lasted till lunch, and this kingdom NEVER ends. Now Mary has a question for the angel.

cards.question: Gabriel has told Mary she'll have a son. What does Mary ask him?

answers.text: How can this be since I am a virgin
Why would God pick someone like me
When exactly will the baby be born

cards.text: Zechariah asked Gabriel a question too, and he walked out unable to say a word (Luke 1:18-22). Mary asks hers, and the angel replies.

cards.question: Gabriel tells Mary how this will happen. Who will come upon her?
The power of the Most High will overshadow Mary, so the Holy One to be born will be called the ___ of God.
Gabriel points Mary to someone in her own family. Which relative of Mary's, once called barren, has conceived a son in her old age?
True or false: Gabriel tells Mary that no word from God will ever fail.

cards.text: My oven has failed, my timer has failed, and I have DEFINITELY failed, but not one word from God ever will. Now it's Mary's turn to answer.

cards.question: Gabriel has told Mary everything. How does Mary answer him?

answers.text: Let me talk to Joseph first
Give me a sign to be sure

cards.text: Then Mary says, “May it happen to me according to your word.” The angel leaves her, and friend, this story is just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Card 1 adds timing the text doesn't give. 'The angel who just told Zechariah' and 'Two huge announcements back to back' make the two visits sound close together. But Elizabeth conceived after Zechariah went home (Luke 1:23-24), and Luke 1:26 puts Gabriel's visit to Mary in the sixth month.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Card 1 says 'In the sixth month' but never says what the six months are counting from. The passage starts in the middle of the earlier story, so the baker has no anchor for that time. The card could say 'six months after Zechariah's wife got pregnant' without naming Elizabeth, so card 16's answer stays hidden.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The wrong answer, True (Mary is already married to Joseph), can be argued as right. In that culture a pledge to marry was legally binding, and Matthew 1:19-20 calls Joseph 'her husband' and Mary 'your wife.' A baker could reasonably argue for True.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Mary and Joseph first appear inside a true or false statement, right after another choice card. No story card tells Luke 1:27 or introduces them first, so the setup for this choice is missing.

rule.text: The setup for a choice is on a story card. Not every choice card needs its own story card right before it: a choice card can follow another choice card when the setup is already told.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. Only 'The throne of His father David' ties the throne to the son's own family, and card 3 already said Joseph is of the house of David. 'Herod king of Judea' and 'Caesar in Rome' have no such link, so the right answer is obvious from its wording.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Most of card 11 retells Luke 1:33 (the kingdom never ends), which card 10 just asked about. Its only new content is 'Now Mary has a question for the angel,' so it works as a recap with a joke instead of telling the next part of the passage.

Card 13 puts Zechariah's question next to Mary's and implies that his asking a question is why he couldn't speak. Luke 1:20 gives the actual reason: 'because you did not believe my words.' Luke never compares the two questions, so the card states a connection the texts don't.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Card 8 already told the baker the baby 'will be called the Son of the Most High.' That gives away the blank in 'will be called the ___ of God,' so the answer Son is already known.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 18 retells Luke 1:37 ('not one word from God ever will' fail), which card 17 just asked about. Apart from that, it only adds 'Now it's Mary's turn to answer.' The joke rides on a recap instead of on a new part of the passage.
